chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥarīz, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about game struck by a shot, which its owner finds the next day: should he eat from it? He said: “If he knows that his shot was what killed it, then let him eat, and that is if he had mentioned the name of Allah.”

key_terms.الرَّمِيَّةِ: game or prey struck by a shot
key_terms.رَمْيَتَهُ: his shot or cast that struck the animal
key_terms.سَمَّى: mentioned the name of Allah at the time of hunting
key_terms.صَاحِبُهَا: its owner, meaning the hunter who shot it

ai.seo_question: Can a hunter eat an animal found the next day after shooting it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding hunted game found after some time has passed. It permits eating from the animal if the hunter is certain that his own shot killed it and if he had invoked the name of Allah at the time of shooting.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4127 - Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Hariz who said:

Abu Abdullah (as), was asked about an animal shot with an arrow, and its owner finds it the next day. Should he eat from it?
Imam (as) said: "If he knows that his shot is what killed it, then he may eat it, provided that he had mentioned the name of Allah (swt) (at the time of shooting)."
